mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% over the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 1 month over the next 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month indicates a contraction in consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS drops > 2% MoM over the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO rises > 1% MoM over the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS rises > 200k over the next 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% month-over-month and retail sales (RSAFS) are stagnant (change < 1% MoM), it indicates a weakening demand side, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops > 10% MoM and RSAFS change < 1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST drops > 10% MoM and RSAFS change < 1% MoM over the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) rises by more than 1% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3%, it signals a strong supply side coupled with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO rises > 1% MoM and FEDFUNDS < 3% over the next 20 trading days.
